```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Snowflake is a hosted SQL data platform. A warehouse supplies the compute
for queries; database roles control access. Add Snowflake data to a Shiny app using each visitor's own account and role.
Query through a DBI connection, or use dbplyr to work with tables.

The example first shows the signed-in user's Snowflake username and role,
so you can check the connection before querying your data.

## Try the guided demo

Run `shinyOAuthDB::oauth_db_cloud_demo("snowflake")` in your R console.
The guide asks for `server`, `role`, `warehouse` and the custom OAuth
`client_id`; it explains how an administrator registers the exact local
callback and where to obtain the client secret. It uses a confidential
integration and masked secret input, or `OAUTHDB_SNOWFLAKE_CLIENT_SECRET`.
Install `odbc`, `processx`, `askpass` and the Snowflake ODBC driver first.

The editable local app requests the same role at sign-in and connection,
then waits for **Run example query**. Queries may resume a warehouse and
consume credits; stopping the app doesn't suspend a shared warehouse.
Optional `database`, `schema` and `driver` arguments customize the setup.
See [Guided cloud demos](cloud-demos.html) for pausing, editing and resuming.

Without an account, check [Snowflake trial accounts](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/admin-trial-account).
You still need permission to create the OAuth integration and a usable
role/warehouse. Live trial compatibility remains unverified here.

## Snowflake setup

In R, run `install.packages("odbc")`, then install the
[Snowflake ODBC driver](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/odbc/odbc)
for your operating system. Ask your administrator for a
[custom-client OAuth integration](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/oauth-custom)
with `http://localhost:8100` as its redirect URI. Users need a role with
access to the warehouse and data.

For this local HTTP callback, the development integration needs
`OAUTH_ALLOW_NON_TLS_REDIRECT_URI = TRUE`. Use an HTTPS callback when
deploying. The [integration settings](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/sql/create-security-integration-oauth-snowflake)
describe this option and refresh-token settings.

Save the integration's client ID and secret in a local `.Renviron` file,
then restart R:

```text
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
```

| Setting | Where to get it |
| --- | --- |
| `server` | Your account's connection details; use its `.snowflakecomputing.com` hostname |
| `warehouse`, `database`, `role` | Names your Snowflake administrator grants to the users |
| Client ID and secret | The custom-client security integration, shown below |

If the integration doesn't exist yet, follow **Create the OAuth integration**
after the app example. Snowflake runs as a cloud service; this guide needs
an account rather than a Docker container.

## A complete app

Save this as `example.R`. Replace the connection settings, keeping the server
and role the same in the sign-in client and connection helper:

```{r app}
library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

client <- oauth_db_snowflake_client(
  server = "organization-account.snowflakecomputing.com",
  role = "REPORTING_READER",
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100"
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
    tableOutput("rows")
  ),
  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  con <- oauth_db_snowflake(
    auth$connection,
    server = "organization-account.snowflakecomputing.com",
    role = "REPORTING_READER",
    warehouse = "REPORTING_WH",
    database = "ANALYTICS"
  )

  output$rows <- renderTable({
    connection <- con()
    DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT CURRENT_USER(), CURRENT_ROLE()")
  })
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server, uiPattern = ".*"),
  port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)

# Open the app in your regular browser at http://localhost:8100
# (viewers in RStudio/Positron/etc. cannot perform necessary redirects)
```

Run `source("example.R")` and open
`http://localhost:8100`. Sign in to run the query; signing out clears the
output.

## Create the OAuth integration

A Snowflake administrator can run this in a SQL worksheet to register a
local development app:

```sql
CREATE SECURITY INTEGRATION shiny_reporting
  TYPE = OAUTH
  ENABLED = TRUE
  OAUTH_CLIENT = CUSTOM
  OAUTH_CLIENT_TYPE = 'CONFIDENTIAL'
  OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI = 'http://localhost:8100'
  OAUTH_ALLOW_NON_TLS_REDIRECT_URI = TRUE
  OAUTH_ENFORCE_PKCE = TRUE
  OAUTH_ISSUE_REFRESH_TOKENS = TRUE;

SELECT SYSTEM$SHOW_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRETS('SHINY_REPORTING');
```

Copy `OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` and `OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` into `.Renviron` as
`OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID` and `OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET`. The integration registers
the app; grant users the reporting role and that role's warehouse/table
permissions separately. Use HTTPS and disable the non-TLS redirect exception
when deploying. Snowflake's [custom-client guide](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/oauth-custom)
covers integration privileges and role restrictions.

## Query a table

Replace the output expression with SQL for your data. For example, if your
table is `ANALYTICS.PUBLIC.ORDERS`:

```{r table-query}
output$rows <- renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT * FROM ANALYTICS.PUBLIC.ORDERS LIMIT 20")
})
```

`con()` gets the current user's connection. Call it inside the render or
reactive expression before using DBI or dbplyr.

## Connection defaults

Set `schema = "PUBLIC"` on the helper to choose a default schema. Omit
`warehouse`, `database`, or `schema` to use the account's defaults.
If the installed ODBC driver has a different name, set `driver`.
See `?oauth_db_snowflake` for the full arguments.

The connection uses the Snowflake driver's HTTPS transport and the visitor's
OAuth token. Protocol and authentication overrides are rejected in `...`.

## External OAuth

If Snowflake uses Entra, Okta, or another external provider for OAuth,
configure a shinyOAuth client for that provider. Request the audience and
role scopes accepted by your Snowflake integration.

Connect with `oauth_db_snowflake()` as above. Set `target` if your client
uses named token targets, and `required_scopes` to the integration's role
scope. For native Snowflake OAuth, the helper derives that scope from
`role`; external providers may use different scope names.
[Authentication and sessions](authorization.html) explains custom targets.
